meta.drug: omega-3 carboxylic acids (Epanova; free-fatty-acid formulation of EPA + DHA), 4 g/day
meta.sponsor: AstraZeneca (academic coordination by Cleveland Clinic C5Research; operations IQVIA)
meta.mechanism: Omega-3 fatty acids (EPA + DHA) lowering triglyceride-rich lipoproteins. No single molecular target: the FDA label says the mechanism 'is not completely understood' and lists inhibition of acyl-CoA:1,2-diacylglycerol acyltransferase, increased hepatic beta-oxidation, decreased hepatic lipogenesis and increased plasma lipoprotein lipase activity (S12); ChEMBL records the mechanism as 'Unknown'. Additional hypothesised anti-inflammatory, antithrombotic and antiarrhythmic effects (S4). target_symbol LPL is used as the human-genetic proxy for the triglyceride-lowering pathway (Ference 2019 LPL Mendelian randomization, S10), not as a confirmed drug target.
meta.modality: small molecule (oral omega-3 free fatty acid mixture, 4 x 1 g capsules daily)
meta.indication: reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events in statin-treated high-risk patients with atherogenic (mixed) dyslipidaemia: TG 180 to <500 mg/dL and low HDL-C, with ASCVD, diabetes plus a risk factor, or high-risk primary prevention

n_randomized.quote: A total of 13 078 patients were randomized at 675 academic and community hospitals in 22 countries
n_randomized.note: 6539 per arm. Press release S2 and design paper S4 give 13,086 enrolled/randomized; registry S3 enrollment 13,078 ACTUAL.

median_followup.quote: At study closure the median patient follow-up was 42.0 months (interquartile range [IQR], 37.5-48.3). Patients were treated with study drug for a median of 38.2 months (IQR, 30.5-44.9).

primary_endpoint.value: Time to first of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina

primary_endpoint.note: Same definition in design paper S4 and registry S3 (5-component MACE).

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Age >=18; statin >=4 weeks with LDL-C <100 mg/dL (or maximally tolerated statin); TG 180 to <500 mg/dL and HDL-C <42 mg/dL (men) / <47 mg/dL (women); high CV risk (ASCVD, diabetes with age threshold plus >=1 risk factor, or high-risk primary prevention); >=50% secondary prevention
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: have atherogenic dyslipidemia, defined as triglyceride levels of 180 to less than 500 mg/dL and high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol levels lower than 42 mg/dL for men or lower than 47 mg/dL for women.
inclusion_key_criteria.note: S1 also: 'At least 50% of randomized patients were required to satisfy criteria for secondary cardiovascular prevention.' Fibrates and weight-loss drugs prohibited; >1 g/day omega-3 supplements excluded.

assumed_rrr.note: Chosen as minimal clinically important difference, not derived from the expected lipid effect. Assumed placebo event rate 4%/year (S1, S4).

stopped_early.quote: On January 8, 2020, when 1384 primary end points had been recorded in 13 078 randomized patients, the independent DMC recommended termination of the trial due to a low probability of demonstrating a clinical benefit of omega-3 CA compared with corn oil. This decision was based on the data crossing the futility boundary prespecified in the group sequential monitoring plan in conjunction with an increased risk of atrial fibrillation

hr.quote: The primary end point occurred in 785 patients (12.0%) treated with omega-3 CA vs 795 (12.2%) treated with corn oil (hazard ratio, 0.99 [95% CI, 0.90-1.09]; P = .84).
hr.note: Registry S3: HR 0.99 (0.90-1.09), p=0.837. Core MACE (CV death/MI/stroke) HR 1.05 (0.93-1.19); CV death HR 1.09 (0.90-1.31); all-cause death HR 1.13 (0.97-1.31) (Table 2). Secondary prevention subgroup HR 0.94 (0.84-1.05), primary prevention 1.16 (0.95-1.41), interaction P=.07.

safety_signals.value: New-onset atrial fibrillation increased: 144 (2.2%) vs 86 (1.3%); HR 1.69 (1.29-2.21)
safety_signals.quote: an increased rate of investigator-reported new-onset atrial fibrillation was observed in the omega-3 CA group (2.2% vs 1.3%; HR, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.29-2.21]; nominal P < .001) compared with corn oil (number needed to harm, 114)
safety_signals.note: Not adjudicated (tertiary end point). Contributed to the DMC stop recommendation together with futility. Similar AF signal in REDUCE-IT (5.3% vs 3.9%) per S1 Discussion.

safety_signals.quote: There were more gastrointestinal adverse events in the omega-3 CA group (24.7%) compared with corn oil–treated patients (14.7%).

safety_signals.value: Discontinuation for adverse events 10.8% vs 8.0%; dose reduction 12.0% vs 6.1%
safety_signals.quote: Discontinuation of study drug treatment (10.8% vs 8.0%) and dose reduction (12.0% vs 6.1%) for adverse events occurred more frequently in patients treated with omega-3 CA compared with those treated with corn oil.

safety_signals.value: No excess bleeding: any bleeding 322 (4.9%) vs 322 (4.9%); TIMI major 0.8% vs 0.7%
safety_signals.quote: it was reassuring to observe no excess bleeding with omega-3 CA, despite the high rate of use of background antiplatelet agents in the study.

safety_signals.value: All-cause death numerically higher: 373 (5.7%) vs 333 (5.1%), HR 1.13 (0.97-1.31), nominal P=.11
safety_signals.quote: All-cause mortality occurred in 373 patients (5.7%) in the omega-3 CA group and 333 (5.1%) in the corn oil group (nominal P = .11).
safety_signals.note: Not significant; exploratory after hierarchical failure.

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: triglyceride-lowering LPL variants and LDL-C-lowering LDLR variants give the same CHD protection per 10 mg/dL lower apoB; triglycerides have no association with CHD after adjusting for apoB, so benefit of TG lowering should be proportional to the absolute apoB change.
genetics.effect: OR 0.771 (0.741-0.802) per 10 mg/dL lower apoB via LPL score (~69.9 mg/dL lower TG); TG adjusted for apoB OR 1.014 (0.965-1.065)
genetics.quote: Triglyceride-lowering LPL variants and LDL-C-lowering LDLR variants were associated with similar lower risk of CHD per unit difference in ApoB. Therefore, the clinical benefit of lowering triglyceride and LDL-C levels may be proportional to the absolute change in ApoB.
genetics.note: PRE-readout (JAMA online 2019-01-29). Abstract read via Europe PMC (PMC6439767 exists). STRENGTH lowered TG 18% with no significant apoB change (GMR 0.99), which under this model predicts almost no benefit.

genetics.finding: Rare APOC3 loss-of-function mutations lower TG by 39% and are associated with 40% lower CHD risk, supporting a causal role of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins
genetics.quote: The risk of coronary heart disease among 498 carriers of any rare APOC3 mutation was 40% lower than the risk among 110,472 noncarriers (odds ratio, 0.60; 95% confidence interval, 0.47 to 0.75; P=4×10(-6)).
genetics.note: PRE-readout. Cited in the STRENGTH design rationale (S4). Lifelong, large TG reduction; omega-3 CA lowered apoC-III only 12% (S1).

genetics.finding: Human genetic evidence specific to the drug's molecular target: NOT FOUND (omega-3 fatty acids have no single defined target; label mechanism 'not completely understood').
genetics.quote: The mechanism of action of EPANOVA is not completely understood.
genetics.note: S12 is the FDA label (2014), not a genetics paper. Genetic evidence on long-chain omega-3 fatty acid levels and CHD was not curated.

consensus_explanation.summary: Experts read STRENGTH as a well-powered, true neutral result: the drug lowered triglycerides about 18% versus corn oil but barely moved the atherogenic particles (non-HDL-C -5%, apoB -1% and not significant, LDL-C +3%), and the trial still collected 1580 of the 1600 planned events, so the authors said underpowering was not the explanation. Lipid-trait modelling in the Copenhagen General Population Study (Doi, Langsted, Nordestgaard), which used the observed changes in triglycerides, LDL-C and CRP, predicted only about a 4% risk reduction for STRENGTH (HR 0.96). That is consistent with the observed HR 0.99 and far below the 15% the trial was powered to detect. This matches Mendelian randomization showing that triglyceride lowering helps only in proportion to apoB lowering (Ference 2019). Exposure-response analyses found no benefit even in patients with the highest achieved EPA levels (top-tertile HR 0.98), arguing against an extra non-lipid benefit of omega-3 fatty acids at this dose. Most of the expert debate is about why REDUCE-IT differed (mineral-oil versus corn-oil comparator, EPA alone versus EPA+DHA, achieved EPA levels), and that question is still open. The trial was stopped for futility, together with an excess of atrial fibrillation (HR 1.69).
consensus_explanation.review_note: 2026-10-23 blind review (without the system's predictions): biomarker_not_causal added as a secondary. Triglycerides fell as intended but apoB did not (ratio 0.99 vs corn oil), and benefit tracks apoB (Ference 2019); the primary stays effect_too_small because triglycerides per se are rated uncertain.

pre_readout.note: Facts with a public source dated before readout_date (2020-01-13).
available_before_readout: Phase 2 ESPRIT (statin-treated, TG 200-500): 4 g/d lowered TG -20.6% vs -5.9% olive oil and non-HDL-C -6.9% vs -0.9%; LDL-C not increased at 4 g (S5, 2013-08-30)
Phase 2 EVOLVE (severe HTG): TG -30.9% at 4 g/d vs -4.3% olive oil; LDL-C increased (S6, 2013-10-14)
FDA label: mechanism not completely understood (S12, 2014)
Registry record with primary endpoint and eligibility (S3, first posted 2014-04-04)
APOC3 loss-of-function genetics: TG-rich lipoproteins causal (S11, 2014-06-18)
Design: ~13,000 patients, 1600 events, 90% power for 15% RRR, two-sided alpha 0.05, 4%/y event rate, interim analyses at 50% and 75% (S4, 2018-09-28)
Ference 2019 MR: benefit of TG lowering proportional to apoB change (S10, 2019-01-29)
only_after_readout: Phase 3 HR 0.99 (0.90-1.09), events 785 vs 795, 12-month placebo-adjusted lipid changes (TG -18%, non-HDL -5%, apoB -1%), AF and GI safety (S1, 2020-11-15)
Copenhagen trial-mimicking biomarker model predicting HR 0.96 for STRENGTH (S8, 2021-08-29) and Maki editorial (S9, 2021-10-02)

access_summary.note: Key numbers: n, median FU, planned events, assumed RRR, power, alpha, baseline LDL-C/TG/HDL-C/non-HDL-C/apoB, TG %, non-HDL %, apoB %, LDL-C %, HDL-C %, HR, CI low/high, p, events x2. All are in the free PMC full text of S1 (PMC7667577); outcome numbers are also in registry results S3. open_questions: Placebo-adjusted ABSOLUTE lipid changes are not reported; change_abs values are DERIVED as (GMR - 1) x baseline median (TG -43 mg/dL = -0.49 mmol/L; non-HDL-C -6.25 mg/dL = -0.16 mmol/L; apoB -0.56 mg/dL; LDL-C +2.25 mg/dL = +0.058 mmol/L). Differences of 12-month medians give similar values (TG -44, non-HDL -7 mg/dL).
Readout date: the DMC recommended stopping on 2020-01-08 (S1), but this was not public; the first public announcement is the AstraZeneca press release of 2020-01-13 07:00 GMT (S2).
Interim HR at the 1384-event futility look was never published; the final HR 0.99 (0.90-1.09) is based on 1580 adjudicated events.
Enrollment count: press release and design paper say 13,086; JAMA paper and registry say 13,078 randomized.
LDL-C assay (Friedewald vs direct) and apoB assay not stated in the main text; baseline apoB (56 mg/dL) is low relative to non-HDL-C (125 mg/dL).

Why REDUCE-IT (HR 0.75 vs mineral oil) differed is unresolved: comparator toxicity (mineral oil raised LDL-C/CRP), EPA alone vs EPA+DHA, higher achieved EPA (144 vs 89 μg/mL), or formulation. Doi et al. explain about half of REDUCE-IT's effect by comparator biomarker changes; Maki suggests corn oil (linoleic acid) may be weakly beneficial.
target_symbol: omega-3 fatty acids have no single molecular target; LPL is used as the genetic proxy for the TG-lowering pathway. Calculator target_genetics set to 'uncertain'.
Press release URL: direct astrazeneca.com URL returns HTTP 403 to curl (readable via WebFetch); the earliest Wayback snapshot is 2020-03-03, not 2020-01-13.
JAMA editorials S13 (Sharma/Martin/Blumenthal) and S14 (Curfman) were not read.
